stimuli.text: Researchers investigated whether caffeine improves attention. They recruited 80 university students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition drank coffee containing 200 milligrams of caffeine. Participants in the other condition drank decaffeinated coffee that tasted the same. The researchers then recorded the number of targets that each participant correctly detected in a ten-minute computer task.

Researchers collected data from 400 high school students. For each one, they recorded the average number of hours slept per night and grade point average. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.45.

Researchers investigated whether the color of a drink affects the ability to identify its flavor. They recruited 70 adult volunteers and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition tasted ten fruit drinks whose colors did not match their flavors. Participants in the other condition tasted the same ten drinks with matching colors. The researchers then recorded the number of flavors out of ten that each participant named correctly.

Researchers collected data from 350 adults. For each one, they recorded the number of stressful life events in the past year and the number of colds in the past year. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.33.

Researchers investigated whether a smiling expression makes cartoons seem funnier. They recruited 90 university students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition held a pen between their teeth, which produces a smile. Participants in the other condition held a pen between their lips, which prevents a smile. The researchers then recorded the rating from 1 to 10 that each participant gave to a set of cartoons.

Researchers investigated whether an expected reward reduces children's later interest in drawing. They recruited 60 preschool children who enjoyed drawing and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Children in one condition were promised a certificate for drawing and received it. Children in the other condition drew with no reward mentioned. The researchers then recorded the number of minutes that each child chose to spend drawing during free time one week later. The results are shown in the table. The difference between the two groups had a p value of 0.41.

rows.group: The group that was promised a certificate
The group that drew without a reward

stimuli.text: Researchers investigated whether agreeing to a small request makes people more likely to agree to a large one. They recruited 120 homeowners and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Homeowners in one condition were first asked to sign a road-safety petition and two weeks later were asked to put a large sign in their garden. Homeowners in the other condition were only asked to put the large sign in their garden. The researchers then recorded the percentage of homeowners in each group who agreed to display the sign.

Researchers collected data from 1,200 teenagers. For each one, they recorded the number of hours of social media use per day and score on a depression questionnaire. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.28.

Researchers investigated whether praise increases hand raising in class. They recruited 50 second-grade students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Children in one condition were praised by the teacher each time they raised a hand before speaking. Children in the other condition received no special response when they raised a hand. The researchers then recorded the number of times that each child raised a hand during one week.

Researchers investigated whether cognitive-behavioral therapy reduces depression. They recruited 90 adults diagnosed with major depressive disorder and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition received twelve weekly sessions of cognitive-behavioral therapy. Participants in the other condition were placed on a waiting list for twelve weeks and were treated afterward. The researchers then recorded each participant's score on a standard depression questionnaire after twelve weeks.

Researchers investigated whether regular aerobic exercise improves memory in older adults. They recruited 100 adults aged 60 to 75 and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition walked briskly for 40 minutes three times a week for six months. Participants in the other condition did gentle stretching for the same amount of time. The researchers then recorded the number of locations that each participant correctly recalled on a spatial memory test.

Read the summary of a hypothetical study, then answer parts A to F.

**Introduction.** Researchers investigated whether a night without sleep slows reaction time. They hypothesized that the amount of sleep would affect reaction time.

**Participants.** The sample was 60 adult volunteers, recruited from one city. All participants gave informed consent, were told they could withdraw at any time, and were debriefed afterward. The plan was approved by an institutional review board.

**Method.** The participants were randomly assigned to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition stayed awake all night in the laboratory. Participants in the other condition slept for eight hours in the laboratory. The researchers recorded the average time in milliseconds that each participant took to press a button when a light appeared.

**Results.** The group that stayed awake all night: mean reaction time (ms) = 412. The group that slept for eight hours: mean reaction time (ms) = 318. The difference was statistically significant (p = 0.01).

Use the three hypothetical sources to answer the question: **Does heavy social media use harm the well-being of teenagers?**

**Source A.** A survey of 1,200 teenagers found a correlation of r = +0.28 between hours of social media use per day and scores on a depression questionnaire. Teenagers who reported feeling lonely tended both to use social media more and to have higher depression scores.

**Source B.** In an experiment, 140 university students were randomly assigned either to limit social media use to 30 minutes a day for three weeks or to continue as usual. At the end, the limited group had a mean loneliness score of 38 and the usual-use group a mean of 45 (p = 0.03).

**Source C.** Researchers interviewed 40 teenagers about their experiences online. Many described feeling worse about themselves after viewing images of peers who seemed more attractive or popular; others described feeling supported by online friends who shared their interests.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the ability to reason quickly and abstractly, which tends to decline in older adulthood?

options.why: Dementia is a serious decline in memory and thinking that interferes with daily life, most common in old age.
Scaffolding is the temporary support that a more skilled person gives a learner and gradually removes.
Crystallized intelligence is the accumulated knowledge and verbal skills that tend to increase with age.
Correct. Fluid intelligence is the ability to reason quickly and abstractly, which tends to decline in older adulthood.

questions.explanation: Fluid intelligence is the ability to reason quickly and abstractly, which tends to decline in older adulthood.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the category of character strengths that includes teamwork, fairness and leadership?

options.why: Courage is the category of character strengths that includes bravery, honesty and perseverance.
Correct. Justice is the category of character strengths that includes teamwork, fairness and leadership.
Wisdom is the category of character strengths that includes creativity, curiosity and love of learning.
Transcendence is the category of character strengths that includes gratitude, hope, humor and appreciation of beauty.

questions.explanation: Justice is the category of character strengths that includes teamwork, fairness and leadership.

questions.stem: Paranoid, schizoid and schizotypal personality disorders belong to which cluster?

options.why: Cluster B is the group of personality disorders marked by dramatic, emotional or erratic behavior: antisocial, borderline, histrionic and narcissistic.
Correct. Cluster A is the group of personality disorders marked by odd or eccentric behavior: paranoid, schizoid and schizotypal.
A personality disorder is a lasting, rigid pattern of behavior and inner experience that differs from cultural expectations and impairs functioning.
Cluster C is the group of personality disorders marked by anxious or fearful behavior: avoidant, dependent and obsessive-compulsive.

questions.explanation: Cluster A is the group of personality disorders marked by odd or eccentric behavior: paranoid, schizoid and schizotypal.

questions.stem: All of the subjects in this study were drawn from one group: 80 university students. What does this most limit?

options.text: Whether the dependent variable was operationally defined
options.why: The measure was clearly defined.

options.text: Whether the study had a control group
options.why: The study had a comparison condition.

options.text: How far the findings can be generalized to other populations
options.why: Correct. A sample that does not represent the wider population limits generalizability.

options.text: Whether a cause-and-effect conclusion can be drawn
options.why: Random assignment, not the sample, allows the causal conclusion.

questions.explanation: A sample that does not represent the wider population limits generalizability.

questions.stem: A psychologist says a client's depression results from inherited genes and low levels of certain neurotransmitters. Which perspective is this?

options.why: The cognitive perspective is the view that disorders result from distorted or irrational ways of thinking.
The sociocultural perspective is the view that disorders result from social and cultural factors, such as poverty and discrimination.
Correct. The biological perspective is the view that disorders result from genetic, brain or chemical causes.
The evolutionary perspective is the view that disorders involve behaviors that once helped survival but are now harmful.

questions.explanation: The biological perspective is the view that disorders result from genetic, brain or chemical causes.

questions.stem: Although he is bright and works hard, ten-year-old Theo reads far below the level expected for his age. Which disorder does this suggest?

options.why: Correct. A specific learning disorder is the neurodevelopmental disorder marked by persistent difficulty in reading, writing or math despite normal intelligence.
Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder is the neurodevelopmental disorder marked by inattention, hyperactivity and impulsiveness.
Autism spectrum disorder is the neurodevelopmental disorder marked by difficulties with social communication and by repetitive behaviors or narrow interests.
Binge-eating disorder is the eating disorder in which a person repeatedly eats very large amounts and feels distress, without purging afterward.

questions.explanation: A specific learning disorder is the neurodevelopmental disorder marked by persistent difficulty in reading, writing or math despite normal intelligence.

questions.stem: Asked about his future, Cole shrugs; he has not thought about it and does not care to. Which identity status is this?

options.why: Correct. Identity diffusion is the identity status of a person who has neither explored options nor made a commitment.
Identity achievement is the identity status of a person who has explored options and made a commitment.
Identity moratorium is the identity status of a person who is actively exploring options but has not yet made a commitment.
Identity foreclosure is the identity status of a person who has made a commitment without exploring options.

questions.explanation: Identity diffusion is the identity status of a person who has neither explored options nor made a commitment.

questions.stem: An expert pool player makes more of her shots when a crowd is watching than when she plays alone. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Deindividuation is the loss of self-awareness and self-restraint in group situations that provide arousal and anonymity.
Diffusion of responsibility is the reduced sense of personal duty to act when other people are present.
Social loafing is the tendency for people to put in less effort when working in a group than when working alone.
Correct. Social facilitation is the improved performance on simple or well-learned tasks in the presence of others.

questions.explanation: Social facilitation is the improved performance on simple or well-learned tasks in the presence of others.

questions.stem: Humanistic psychologists argue that people are naturally motivated to become the best version of themselves. What is this motivation called?

options.why: A defense mechanism is in psychodynamic theory, a method the ego uses without awareness to reduce anxiety by distorting reality.
A projective test is a personality test, such as an inkblot test, that asks people to interpret unclear images in order to reveal hidden feelings.
Unconditional positive regard is the attitude of total acceptance toward another person, whatever they say or do.
Correct. The self-actualizing tendency is in humanistic theory, the inborn drive of people to grow and fulfill their potential.

questions.explanation: The self-actualizing tendency is in humanistic theory, the inborn drive of people to grow and fulfill their potential.

questions.stem: To find the pasta sauce, a shopper skips most aisles and goes straight to the aisle with the pasta. Which problem-solving strategy is she using?

options.why: Divergent thinking is thinking that produces many possible answers to a problem.
Executive functions is the mental processes used to plan, organize and carry out goal-directed behavior.
An algorithm is a step-by-step procedure that guarantees a solution.
Correct. A heuristic is a simple thinking shortcut that is fast but can lead to errors.

questions.explanation: A heuristic is a simple thinking shortcut that is fast but can lead to errors.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a possible third variable that could explain the correlation?

options.why: This is the statistic, not a variable.
This is one of the two variables that were measured.

options.text: The level of stress at home
options.why: Correct. A third variable could influence both measures and so produce the correlation.

options.text: The average number of hours slept per night
options.why: This is one of the two variables that were measured.

questions.explanation: A third variable could influence both measures and so produce the correlation.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes sampling bias?

options.text: A flaw in selecting participants that makes the sample unlike the population
options.why: Correct. This is what sampling bias means.

options.text: A sample whose characteristics match those of the population it is drawn from
options.why: That describes a representative sample.

options.text: A sample made up of whoever is easiest for the researcher to reach
options.why: That describes a convenience sample.

options.text: The selecting of participants so that every member of the population has an equal chance of being chosen
options.why: That describes random sampling.

questions.explanation: Sampling bias is a flaw in selecting participants that makes the sample unlike the population.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes a hallucinogen?

options.text: A drug, such as alcohol, that slows neural activity and body functions
options.why: That describes a depressant.

options.text: A drug, such as marijuana, that distorts perception and can cause sensory experiences without sensory input
options.why: Correct. This is what a hallucinogen means.

options.text: A drug, such as caffeine or cocaine, that speeds up neural activity and body functions
options.why: That describes a stimulant.

options.text: A drug, such as heroin, that relieves pain by acting on endorphin receptors and is highly addictive
options.why: That describes an opioid.

questions.explanation: A hallucinogen is a drug, such as marijuana, that distorts perception and can cause sensory experiences without sensory input.

questions.stem: Karl, who dislikes his colleague, is convinced that the colleague hates him. Which defense mechanism is this?

options.why: Denial is the defense mechanism of refusing to accept a painful reality.
Displacement is the defense mechanism of shifting an impulse from its real target to a safer one.
Correct. Projection is the defense mechanism of seeing one's own unacceptable impulses in other people.
Rationalization is the defense mechanism of giving a comfortable excuse in place of the real reason for a behavior.

questions.explanation: Projection is the defense mechanism of seeing one's own unacceptable impulses in other people.

questions.stem: As a friend walks away, her image on Tom's retina shrinks, but he does not think she is getting smaller. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Apparent movement is the perception of motion when a series of still images or lights is shown in quick succession.
Color constancy is the perception that an object keeps the same color under different lighting.
Shape constancy is the perception that an object keeps the same shape even when the viewing angle changes.
Correct. Size constancy is the perception that an object keeps the same size even when its image on the retina changes.

questions.explanation: Size constancy is the perception that an object keeps the same size even when its image on the retina changes.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes nature and nurture?

options.text: The developmental question of how heredity and experience together shape a person
options.why: Correct. This is what nature and nurture means.

options.text: Research that compares people of different ages at one point in time
options.why: That describes a cross-sectional study.

options.text: The view that development happens in distinct stages, like a staircase
options.why: That describes discontinuous development.

options.text: The developmental question of which traits stay the same through life and which ones alter
options.why: That describes stability and change.

questions.explanation: Nature and nurture is the developmental question of how heredity and experience together shape a person.

questions.stem: Why did the researchers assign the participants to the two conditions at random?

options.text: So that the results could be generalized to the whole population
options.why: That is the purpose of random sampling, not random assignment.

options.text: So that the two groups would be similar at the start, and any difference could be attributed to the independent variable
options.why: Correct. Random assignment spreads individual differences evenly across the conditions.

options.text: So that the study would have more participants
options.why: Random assignment does not change the sample size.

options.text: So that nobody would know the hypothesis
options.why: That describes a blind procedure.

questions.explanation: Random assignment spreads individual differences evenly across the conditions.

questions.stem: When two brothers fight over a game, their father removes the game, and the fighting decreases. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Negative reinforcement is the strengthening of a behavior by removing an unpleasant stimulus after it.
Positive punishment is the weakening of a behavior by adding an unpleasant stimulus after it.
Correct. Negative punishment is the weakening of a behavior by removing a pleasant stimulus after it.
Positive reinforcement is the strengthening of a behavior by adding a pleasant stimulus after it.

questions.explanation: Negative punishment is the weakening of a behavior by removing a pleasant stimulus after it.

questions.stem: A second study of a different pair of measures finds r = −0.53. Which relationship is stronger?

options.text: Neither, because relationships with different signs cannot be compared
options.why: Strength can be compared by distance from zero.

options.text: The relationship in the first study, because its coefficient is closer to zero
options.why: A coefficient closer to zero shows a weaker relationship.

options.text: The relationship with the positive sign, whatever its size
options.why: The sign shows direction, not strength.

options.text: The relationship in the second study, because its coefficient is farther from zero
options.why: Correct. The strength of a correlation is its distance from zero, whatever the sign.

questions.explanation: The strength of a correlation is its distance from zero, whatever the sign.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes a morpheme?

options.text: The whole system of rules in a language that lets people communicate
options.why: That describes grammar.

options.text: The rules by which we get meaning from words and sentences
options.why: That describes semantics.

options.text: The smallest distinctive unit of sound in a language
options.why: That describes a phoneme.

options.text: The smallest unit of language that carries meaning
options.why: Correct. This is what a morpheme means.

questions.explanation: A morpheme is the smallest unit of language that carries meaning.

questions.stem: Which lobes, located at the top and rear of the head, receive sensory input for touch and body position?

options.why: Correct. The parietal lobes is the lobes at the top of the head, which process touch and spatial information.
The frontal lobes is the lobes behind the forehead, which handle planning, judgment and voluntary movement.
The somatosensory cortex is the strip at the front of the parietal lobes that registers touch and body sensations.
The prefrontal cortex is the front part of the frontal lobes, which handles executive functions such as planning and self-control.

questions.explanation: The parietal lobes is the lobes at the top of the head, which process touch and spatial information.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as a state of extreme energy, overconfidence, racing thoughts and little need for sleep?

options.why: Persistent depressive disorder is the disorder in which a person has a mildly depressed mood on most days for at least two years.
Bipolar I disorder is the disorder in which a person has full manic episodes, usually alternating with depression.
Bipolar II disorder is the disorder in which a person alternates between depression and a milder form of mania called hypomania.
Correct. Mania is a state of extreme energy, overconfidence, racing thoughts and little need for sleep.

questions.explanation: Mania is a state of extreme energy, overconfidence, racing thoughts and little need for sleep.

questions.stem: A doctor prescribes a drug that blocks dopamine receptors to reduce a patient's hallucinations. Which kind of drug is this?

options.why: Tardive dyskinesia is the involuntary movements of the face and tongue that can result from long-term use of antipsychotic drugs.
An antianxiety drug is a drug that reduces tension by depressing central nervous system activity and can be addictive.
Correct. An antipsychotic drug is a drug that reduces hallucinations and delusions by blocking dopamine receptors.
An antidepressant is a drug, such as an SSRI, that treats depression and anxiety by raising the availability of serotonin or norepinephrine.

questions.explanation: An antipsychotic drug is a drug that reduces hallucinations and delusions by blocking dopamine receptors.

questions.stem: A driver cuts in front of Ruth, and she immediately concludes he is a rude person, never considering that he may be rushing to a hospital. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: The self-serving bias is the tendency to credit our successes to ourselves and blame our failures on outside factors.
An optimistic explanatory style is the habit of explaining bad events as temporary, specific and caused by outside factors.
Correct. The fundamental attribution error is the tendency, when judging other people's behavior, to overestimate personal traits and underestimate the situation.
A pessimistic explanatory style is the habit of explaining bad events as lasting, affecting everything and caused by oneself.

questions.explanation: The fundamental attribution error is the tendency, when judging other people's behavior, to overestimate personal traits and underestimate the situation.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes amplitude?

options.text: The distance from one wave peak to the next, which determines the hue of light
options.why: That describes wavelength.

options.text: The height of a sound wave, which determines loudness
options.why: Correct. This is what amplitude means.

options.text: The coiled, fluid-filled tube in the inner ear where sound waves become neural impulses
options.why: That describes the cochlea.

options.text: The number of sound waves per second, which determines pitch
options.why: That describes frequency.

questions.explanation: Amplitude is the height of a sound wave, which determines loudness.

questions.stem: Which part of the brain is the thin outer layer responsible for higher-order thinking?

options.why: Correct. The cerebral cortex is the wrinkled outer layer of the brain, which handles thinking, perception and voluntary movement.
The hypothalamus is the structure that regulates hunger, thirst, body temperature and sexual behavior and controls the pituitary gland.
The corpus callosum is the band of fibers that connects the two hemispheres of the brain.
The hippocampus is the structure that forms new explicit memories of facts and events.

questions.explanation: The cerebral cortex is the wrinkled outer layer of the brain, which handles thinking, perception and voluntary movement.

questions.stem: Six dots are drawn as three close pairs, and people see three groups rather than six dots. Which Gestalt principle explains this?

options.why: Figure and ground is the Gestalt principle that we organize a scene into an object that stands out and its background.
Closure is the Gestalt principle that we fill in gaps to see a complete, whole object.
Correct. Proximity is the Gestalt principle that we group together objects that are near each other.
Similarity is the Gestalt principle that we group together objects that look alike.

questions.explanation: Proximity is the Gestalt principle that we group together objects that are near each other.

questions.stem: An elderly woman's memory steadily worsens over several years until she no longer recognizes her family. Which condition does she most likely have?

options.why: Infantile amnesia is the inability of adults to remember events from the first few years of life.
Retrograde amnesia is the loss of memories from before an injury or illness.
Correct. Alzheimer's disease is a progressive brain disease that destroys memory and then other mental abilities.
Anterograde amnesia is the inability to form new memories after an injury or illness.

questions.explanation: Alzheimer's disease is a progressive brain disease that destroys memory and then other mental abilities.

questions.stem: Students catch more colds during exam weeks than at other times of year. Which effect of stress best explains this?

options.why: Problem-focused coping is the reducing of stress by changing the stressor itself or the way one deals with it.
Emotion-focused coping is the reducing of stress by managing one's emotional reaction rather than the stressor.
Correct. Immune suppression is the weakening of the body's defenses against illness during long-term stress.
Hypertension is persistently high blood pressure, which is made more likely by chronic stress.

questions.explanation: Immune suppression is the weakening of the body's defenses against illness during long-term stress.

questions.stem: Yara loves trying unfamiliar foods, visiting art galleries and exploring new ideas. She would score high on which Big Five trait?

options.why: Correct. Openness to experience is the Big Five trait of being imaginative, curious and willing to try new things.
Conscientiousness is the Big Five trait of being organized, careful and self-disciplined.
Emotional stability is the Big Five trait of being calm and secure rather than anxious and moody.
Extraversion is the Big Five trait of being sociable, outgoing and energetic.

questions.explanation: Openness to experience is the Big Five trait of being imaginative, curious and willing to try new things.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes mood-congruent memory?

options.text: The improved recall that occurs in the same physical state as when the information was learned
options.why: That describes state-dependent memory.

options.text: A stimulus that helps bring a memory to mind
options.why: That describes a retrieval cue.

options.text: The tendency to recall memories that match one's current mood
options.why: Correct. This is what mood-congruent memory means.

options.text: The retrieval of information without any cues, as in an essay question
options.why: That describes recall.

questions.explanation: Mood-congruent memory is the tendency to recall memories that match one's current mood.

questions.stem: After surviving a serious illness, Vera reports closer relationships, a greater appreciation of life and a new sense of purpose. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Signature strengths is the positive character traits, such as kindness or curiosity, that are most central to a particular person.
Subjective well-being is a person's own evaluation of how happy and satisfied they are with life.
Correct. Posttraumatic growth is the positive psychological change that some people experience after struggling with a very difficult event.
Gratitude is the appreciation of the good things in one's life, the practice of which raises well-being.

questions.explanation: Posttraumatic growth is the positive psychological change that some people experience after struggling with a very difficult event.

questions.stem: Hallucinations and delusions are experiences that are present in schizophrenia but absent in healthy functioning. Which kind of symptom are they?

options.why: Correct. A positive symptom is a symptom of schizophrenia that adds an inappropriate behavior or experience, such as hallucinations.
The dopamine hypothesis is the idea that schizophrenia involves excessive activity of the neurotransmitter dopamine.
A negative symptom is a symptom of schizophrenia that takes away a normal behavior, such as emotional expression or motivation.
An acute onset is the sudden appearance of schizophrenia, often after stress, from which recovery is more likely.

questions.explanation: A positive symptom is a symptom of schizophrenia that adds an inappropriate behavior or experience, such as hallucinations.

questions.stem: On a dark night, Kai can make out shapes but not colors. Which receptor cells is he relying on?

options.why: Correct. Rods is the receptor cells that detect black, white and gray and work in dim light and peripheral vision.
The fovea is the central point of the retina, where cones are packed most densely and vision is sharpest.
The lens is the transparent structure that changes shape to focus light on the retina.
The blind spot is the point where the optic nerve leaves the eye, which has no receptor cells.

questions.explanation: Rods is the receptor cells that detect black, white and gray and work in dim light and peripheral vision.

questions.stem: With her eyes closed, Uma can still touch her nose with her fingertip. Which sense makes this possible?

options.why: Correct. Kinesthesis is the sense of the position and movement of body parts, based on receptors in muscles and joints.
The gate control theory is the theory that the spinal cord has a gate that can block pain signals or let them pass to the brain.
The vestibular sense is the sense of balance and head position, based on the semicircular canals of the inner ear.
Phantom limb sensation is the feeling of pain or touch in a limb that has been amputated.

questions.explanation: Kinesthesis is the sense of the position and movement of body parts, based on receptors in muscles and joints.

questions.stem: A dentist's drill causes pain, and soon the sound of the drill alone makes Ben tense. In this example, the pain is which of the following?

options.why: Correct. The unconditioned stimulus is in classical conditioning, the stimulus that triggers a response naturally, without learning.
The conditioned stimulus is in classical conditioning, the originally neutral stimulus that triggers a response after being paired with another stimulus.
The unconditioned response is in classical conditioning, the natural, unlearned response to a stimulus.
The conditioned response is in classical conditioning, the learned response to a previously neutral stimulus.

questions.explanation: The unconditioned stimulus is in classical conditioning, the stimulus that triggers a response naturally, without learning.

questions.stem: Researchers find that answers to questions about being talkative, sociable and outgoing all rise and fall together, which suggests a single trait. Which statistical method reveals such clusters?

options.why: Correct. Factor analysis is the statistical method that finds clusters of related test items, used to identify basic traits.
Self-efficacy is the belief in one's own ability to succeed at a particular task.
Self-esteem is a person's overall feeling of self-worth.
Reciprocal determinism is the idea that a person's behavior, thoughts and environment all influence one another.

questions.explanation: Factor analysis is the statistical method that finds clusters of related test items, used to identify basic traits.

questions.stem: Why did the researchers assign the participants to the two conditions at random?

options.text: So that the results could be generalized to the whole population
options.why: That is the purpose of random sampling, not random assignment.

options.text: So that the two groups would be similar at the start, and any difference could be attributed to the independent variable
options.why: Correct. Random assignment spreads individual differences evenly across the conditions.

options.text: So that the study would have more participants
options.why: Random assignment does not change the sample size.

options.text: So that nobody would know the hypothesis
options.why: That describes a blind procedure.

questions.explanation: Random assignment spreads individual differences evenly across the conditions.

questions.stem: Which statement about the results is best supported?

options.text: The difference between the groups is statistically significant
options.why: A p value of 0.41 is far above 0.05.

options.text: The study shows that the two conditions always give identical results
options.why: A non-significant result does not show that there is no effect at all.

options.text: The difference between the groups is not statistically significant, so it could easily be due to chance
options.why: Correct. A p value above 0.05 means a difference this size would often occur by chance alone.

options.text: The independent variable had a large effect
options.why: The averages are close and the difference is not significant.

questions.explanation: A p value above 0.05 means a difference this size would often occur by chance alone.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes a survey?

options.text: A testable prediction about the relationship between variables
options.why: That describes a hypothesis.

options.text: The research method in which a researcher manipulates a variable and randomly assigns participants, which allows conclusions about cause and effect
options.why: That describes an experiment.

options.text: The research method of collecting self-reported attitudes or behaviors from a sample by asking questions
options.why: Correct. This is what a survey means.

options.text: The repeating of a study with different participants to see whether the finding holds
options.why: That describes replication.

questions.explanation: A survey is the research method of collecting self-reported attitudes or behaviors from a sample by asking questions.

questions.stem: Because his neighbor looked after his cat last month, Abe feels he should help the neighbor move house. Which norm is guiding him?

options.why: The social responsibility norm is the expectation that people will help those who need help, even at a cost to themselves.
The bystander effect is the tendency for a person to be less likely to help when other people are present.
Altruism is unselfish concern for the welfare of others.
Correct. The social reciprocity norm is the expectation that people will help those who have helped them.

questions.explanation: The social reciprocity norm is the expectation that people will help those who have helped them.

questions.stem: Dana pictures the layout of her house to count the windows. Which part of working memory is she using?

options.why: The central executive is the part of working memory that directs attention and coordinates the other parts.
Correct. The visuospatial sketchpad is the part of working memory that briefly holds images and spatial information.
Long-term potentiation is the strengthening of the connections between neurons after repeated activation, which is the biological basis of memory.
The phonological loop is the part of working memory that briefly holds spoken and written words.

questions.explanation: The visuospatial sketchpad is the part of working memory that briefly holds images and spatial information.

questions.stem: A sound reaches Lena's right ear a split second before her left ear, so she knows the car is on her right. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Frequency theory is the theory that we hear pitch because the rate of nerve impulses matches the frequency of the sound.
Volley theory is the theory that groups of neurons take turns firing so that together they match high sound frequencies.
Conduction deafness is hearing loss caused by damage to the eardrum or the bones of the middle ear.
Correct. Sound localization is the ability to tell where a sound comes from, using differences in timing and loudness between the two ears.

questions.explanation: Sound localization is the ability to tell where a sound comes from, using differences in timing and loudness between the two ears.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the increased confidence that an event happened after repeatedly imagining it?

options.why: Correct. Imagination inflation is the increased confidence that an event happened after repeatedly imagining it.
Source amnesia is the inability to remember where, when or how a piece of information was learned.
Constructive memory is the building of a memory at retrieval from stored pieces, expectations and later information.
The misinformation effect is the distortion of a memory by misleading information received after the event.

questions.explanation: Imagination inflation is the increased confidence that an event happened after repeatedly imagining it.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the arrangement in which each hemisphere controls the opposite side of the body?

options.why: Correct. Contralateral control is the arrangement in which each hemisphere controls the opposite side of the body.
Hemispheric specialization is the tendency for each side of the brain to handle certain functions, such as language in the left hemisphere.
Wernicke's area is the area in the left temporal lobe that controls language comprehension.
Aphasia is an impairment of language caused by brain damage.

questions.explanation: Contralateral control is the arrangement in which each hemisphere controls the opposite side of the body.

questions.stem: A medication prevents the sending neuron from taking serotonin back, so more serotonin stays in the synapse. The medication is acting as which of the following?

options.why: Correct. A reuptake inhibitor is a drug that keeps a neurotransmitter in the synapse longer by blocking its reabsorption.
Tolerance is the need for larger doses of a drug to get the same effect after repeated use.
An antagonist is a drug that decreases the action of a neurotransmitter, for example by blocking its receptors.
Withdrawal is the unpleasant physical and psychological symptoms that follow stopping an addictive drug.

questions.explanation: A reuptake inhibitor is a drug that keeps a neurotransmitter in the synapse longer by blocking its reabsorption.

questions.stem: In one culture, wearing skirts is considered masculine; in another, it is considered feminine. This difference best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Sexual orientation is the direction of a person's enduring sexual attraction.
Sex is the biological characteristics, such as chromosomes and anatomy, by which people are classified as male, female or intersex.
Gender identity is a person's own sense of being male, female, neither or some combination.
Correct. Gender is the socially and culturally influenced attitudes, feelings and behaviors that a culture links to being a boy, girl, man or woman.

questions.explanation: Gender is the socially and culturally influenced attitudes, feelings and behaviors that a culture links to being a boy, girl, man or woman.

questions.stem: What is the independent variable in this study?

options.why: This was measured, not manipulated: it is the dependent variable.
This is a procedure for forming the groups, not a variable.

options.text: The number of participants in the study
options.why: This is the sample size, not a variable the researchers changed.

options.text: Whether a small request came first
options.why: Correct. The independent variable is the factor the researchers changed between the two conditions.

questions.explanation: The independent variable is the factor the researchers changed between the two conditions.

questions.stem: After the election result is announced, Tom says, 'I knew all along that she would win,' although he had predicted the opposite. Which bias is this?

options.why: Correct. Hindsight bias is the tendency, after learning an outcome, to believe one would have predicted it.
Overconfidence is the tendency to be more certain than correct about one's own judgments.
Social desirability bias is the tendency of participants to answer in a way that makes them look good.
Experimenter bias is the influence of a researcher's expectations on the results of a study.

questions.explanation: Hindsight bias is the tendency, after learning an outcome, to believe one would have predicted it.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes a social trap?

options.text: A situation in which people who each pursue their own interest end up harming everyone
options.why: Correct. This is what a social trap means.

options.text: The adjusting of behavior or thinking to match a group standard
options.why: That describes conformity.

options.text: The following of the direct commands of an authority figure
options.why: That describes obedience.

options.text: The view that the different cultural groups in a society should be valued and should keep their identities
options.why: That describes multiculturalism.

questions.explanation: A social trap is a situation in which people who each pursue their own interest end up harming everyone.

questions.stem: In a drug trial, some patients receive a sugar pill that looks exactly like the real medication. The sugar pill is which of the following?

options.why: A double-blind procedure is a procedure in which neither the participants nor the researchers who deal with them know who is in which condition.
The control group is the group in an experiment that does not receive the treatment and is used for comparison.
Correct. A placebo is an inactive substance or treatment that looks like the real one.
The placebo effect is an improvement that results from a person's expectation of a treatment rather than from the treatment itself.

questions.explanation: A placebo is an inactive substance or treatment that looks like the real one.

questions.stem: A child's parents and teachers meet regularly and work together. In ecological systems theory, this connection is part of which system?

options.why: The chronosystem is in ecological systems theory, the life stage and historical events that affect a child.
The exosystem is in ecological systems theory, the settings that affect a child indirectly, such as a parent's workplace.
Correct. The mesosystem is in ecological systems theory, the relationships between the groups in a child's immediate surroundings.
The macrosystem is in ecological systems theory, the cultural values, laws and customs that surround a child.

questions.explanation: The mesosystem is in ecological systems theory, the relationships between the groups in a child's immediate surroundings.

questions.stem: Which research method did the researchers use?

options.why: No variable was manipulated and there was no random assignment.
Correct. The researchers measured two variables and examined their relationship without manipulating anything.
A meta-analysis combines the results of many studies.
A case study examines one individual in depth.

questions.explanation: The researchers measured two variables and examined their relationship without manipulating anything.

questions.stem: Which term refers to the first ejaculation, which marks sexual maturity in boys?

options.why: Menopause is the natural end of menstruation and of the ability to reproduce, usually around age 50.
Menarche is a girl's first menstrual period.
Primary sex characteristics is the body structures, such as ovaries and testes, that make reproduction possible.
Correct. Spermarche is a boy's first ejaculation.

questions.explanation: Spermarche is a boy's first ejaculation.

questions.stem: Scores on a test are normally distributed with a mean of 500 and a standard deviation of 15. About what percentage of scores are between 485 and 515?

options.why: This does not match the 68–95 rule for a normal distribution.
This does not match the 68–95 rule for a normal distribution.
Correct. About 68% of scores fall within one standard deviation of the mean.
This does not match the 68–95 rule for a normal distribution.

questions.explanation: About 68% of scores fall within one standard deviation of the mean. (485 and 515 are one standard deviation from the mean; 470 and 530 are two.)

questions.stem: A psychologist notes that people who score high on verbal tests also tend to score high on spatial and numerical tests, and concludes that one ability underlies them all. Which idea is this?

options.why: The Flynn effect is the steady rise in average intelligence test scores over the generations.
Correct. General intelligence is the single underlying mental ability that Spearman believed affects performance on all mental tasks.
Multiple intelligences is the theory that people have several independent kinds of intelligence, such as musical and interpersonal.
Mental age is the level of performance typical of a certain chronological age on an intelligence test.

questions.explanation: General intelligence is the single underlying mental ability that Spearman believed affects performance on all mental tasks.

questions.stem: Seven students took a memory test. Their scores were 14, 5, 10, 7, 20, 10, 11. What is the mean of the scores?

options.why: That is the median.
Correct. Add the scores (77) and divide by 7.
That is the range.
That is the highest score.

questions.explanation: In order, the scores are 5, 7, 10, 10, 11, 14, 20. Add the scores (77) and divide by 7. The one very high score pulls the mean (11) above the median (10), so the distribution is positively skewed.

questions.stem: Grandpa tells detailed stories about his wedding day and his first job. Which kind of memory is he drawing on?

options.why: Correct. Autobiographical memory is the memory of the events of one's own life.
Maintenance rehearsal is the repeating of information over and over to keep it in short-term memory.
Elaborative rehearsal is the linking of new information to existing knowledge and meaning to store it in long-term memory.
Highly superior autobiographical memory is the rare ability to recall almost every day of one's life in detail.

questions.explanation: Autobiographical memory is the memory of the events of one's own life.

questions.stem: After ten years without cycling, Raj gets on a bicycle and rides without thinking about it. Which kind of memory is this?

options.why: Semantic memory is the explicit memory of facts and general knowledge.
Episodic memory is the explicit memory of personally experienced events.
Prospective memory is the memory to carry out a planned action in the future.
Correct. Procedural memory is the implicit memory of how to perform skills and actions.

questions.explanation: Procedural memory is the implicit memory of how to perform skills and actions.

questions.stem: Which of the following would be a confounding variable in this study?

options.text: The two groups differed in hand raising at the end of the study
options.why: That is the dependent variable, the result being measured.

options.text: One group differed from the other in praise from the teacher
options.why: That is the independent variable itself.

options.text: Each one was assigned to a condition at random
options.why: Random assignment reduces confounding; it is not a confound.

options.text: The praised children were taught in a much smaller class
options.why: Correct. It differs between the groups along with the independent variable, so it could explain the results instead.

questions.explanation: It differs between the groups along with the independent variable, so it could explain the results instead.

questions.stem: A four-year-old enjoys pretend play and talks well, but thinks a tall glass holds more juice than a wide glass with the same amount. Which of Piaget's stages is he in?

options.why: The sensorimotor stage is Piaget's stage from birth to about age 2, in which infants know the world through senses and actions.
Correct. The preoperational stage is Piaget's stage from about age 2 to 7, in which children use words and images but cannot yet reason logically.
The concrete operational stage is Piaget's stage from about age 7 to 11, in which children think logically about real objects and events.
The formal operational stage is Piaget's stage from about age 12 on, in which people can reason about abstract and hypothetical ideas.

questions.explanation: The preoperational stage is Piaget's stage from about age 2 to 7, in which children use words and images but cannot yet reason logically.

questions.stem: Without ever being taught, salmon swim back to the stream where they hatched in order to breed. Which theory of motivation best explains this?

options.why: Correct. Instinct theory is the theory that behavior is driven by fixed, inborn patterns that are not learned.
Drive-reduction theory is the theory that a physical need creates a state of tension that motivates behavior to reduce it.
Self-determination theory is the theory that people are motivated by needs for competence, autonomy and relatedness, either from within or from outside.
Arousal theory is the theory that people are motivated to keep an ideal level of alertness and stimulation.

questions.explanation: Instinct theory is the theory that behavior is driven by fixed, inborn patterns that are not learned.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the deep encoding of a word based on its meaning?

options.why: Structural encoding is the shallow encoding of a word based on its appearance.
Phonemic encoding is the encoding of a word based on its sound.
Correct. Semantic encoding is the deep encoding of a word based on its meaning.
Implicit memory is the memory of skills and learned associations that is retained without conscious recall.

questions.explanation: Semantic encoding is the deep encoding of a word based on its meaning.

questions.stem: A tourist calls another country's eating customs 'wrong' because they differ from the customs at home. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: A stereotype is a generalized belief about a group of people.
Discrimination is unjustified negative behavior toward a group and its members.
Correct. Ethnocentrism is the tendency to judge other cultures by the standards of one's own culture.
The just-world phenomenon is the tendency to believe that people get what they deserve.

questions.explanation: Ethnocentrism is the tendency to judge other cultures by the standards of one's own culture.

questions.stem: Rats that wandered a maze with no reward for ten days ran it almost perfectly as soon as food was placed at the end. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Correct. Latent learning is learning that takes place without reinforcement and is not shown until there is a reason to show it.
A cognitive map is a mental picture of the layout of one's surroundings.
Modeling is the process of demonstrating a behavior that others then observe and imitate.
Vicarious conditioning is learning from seeing the consequences of another person's behavior.

questions.explanation: Latent learning is learning that takes place without reinforcement and is not shown until there is a reason to show it.

questions.stem: Which group served as the control group?

options.text: The group on the waiting list
options.why: Correct. The control group is the comparison group that does not receive the treatment being tested.

options.text: Neither group, because the study had no comparison condition
options.why: The second condition is the comparison.
Only the comparison group is the control group.
This group received the treatment being tested: it is the experimental group.

questions.explanation: The control group is the comparison group that does not receive the treatment being tested.

questions.stem: A dog already salivates to a tone. A light is then repeatedly shown just before the tone, and the dog begins to salivate to the light. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Correct. Higher-order conditioning is the pairing of a new neutral stimulus with an existing conditioned stimulus to create a second conditioned stimulus.
Stimulus discrimination is the learned ability to respond to the conditioned stimulus but not to similar stimuli.
Stimulus generalization is the tendency to respond to stimuli that are similar to the conditioned stimulus.
Spontaneous recovery is the reappearance of a weakened conditioned response after a rest period.

questions.explanation: Higher-order conditioning is the pairing of a new neutral stimulus with an existing conditioned stimulus to create a second conditioned stimulus.

questions.stem: After being told that a blurry photo shows a monster, people looking at it report seeing a monster rather than a log. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Top-down processing is perception that is guided by experience, expectations and context.
The cocktail party effect is the ability to notice personally important information, such as your name, in an unattended conversation.
Selective attention is the focusing of awareness on one stimulus while ignoring others.
Correct. A perceptual set is a readiness to perceive something in a particular way because of expectations.

questions.explanation: A perceptual set is a readiness to perceive something in a particular way because of expectations.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes sensory interaction?

options.text: The reduced sensitivity that follows constant, unchanging stimulation
options.why: That describes sensory adaptation.

options.text: The conversion of physical energy, such as light or sound, into neural impulses
options.why: That describes transduction.

options.text: The way one sense influences another, as when smell affects taste
options.why: Correct. This is what sensory interaction means.

options.text: The weakest level of a stimulus that a person can detect half of the time
options.why: That describes the absolute threshold.

questions.explanation: Sensory interaction is the way one sense influences another, as when smell affects taste.

questions.stem: People who have just read words about old age walk more slowly down a hallway without knowing why. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Correct. Priming is the activation, often without awareness, of certain associations that then influence perception or behavior.
Framing is the way the wording of an issue affects decisions and judgments.
The sunk-cost fallacy is the tendency to keep investing in something because of what has already been spent on it.
The availability heuristic is the judging of how likely something is by how easily examples come to mind.

questions.explanation: Priming is the activation, often without awareness, of certain associations that then influence perception or behavior.

questions.stem: Neither the participants nor the assistants who recorded the results knew which condition each participant was in. What is this procedure called?

options.why: Random sampling is how participants are chosen from a population.
That is a therapy technique, not a research control.
Correct. Keeping both participants and researchers unaware of the conditions reduces bias from expectations.
In a single-blind procedure only the participants are unaware.

questions.explanation: Keeping both participants and researchers unaware of the conditions reduces bias from expectations.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes psychotropic medication?

options.text: Any drug that acts on the brain to treat the symptoms of a psychological disorder
options.why: Correct. This is what psychotropic medication means.

options.text: The treatment for severe depression in which a brief electric current is passed through the brain of an anesthetized patient
options.why: That describes electroconvulsive therapy.

options.text: The treatment in which repeated magnetic pulses are applied to the surface of the brain to treat depression
options.why: That describes transcranial magnetic stimulation.

options.text: The now-abandoned form of psychosurgery that cut the nerves connecting the frontal lobes to the rest of the brain
options.why: That describes a lobotomy.

questions.explanation: Psychotropic medication is any drug that acts on the brain to treat the symptoms of a psychological disorder.

questions.stem: A nine-year-old takes pride in finishing his school projects well and compares his work with classmates' work. Which of Erikson's stages is this?

options.why: Correct. Industry versus inferiority is Erikson's stage in elementary school, in which children learn to feel competent or else feel inadequate.
Trust versus mistrust is Erikson's stage in infancy, in which babies learn whether their needs will be met.
Autonomy versus shame and doubt is Erikson's stage in toddlerhood, in which children learn to do things for themselves.
Initiative versus guilt is Erikson's stage in the preschool years, in which children learn to start tasks and carry out plans.

questions.explanation: Industry versus inferiority is Erikson's stage in elementary school, in which children learn to feel competent or else feel inadequate.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as a lack of emotional expression in the face and voice?

options.why: Disorganized speech is the jumbled, illogical speech, sometimes called word salad, that is a symptom of schizophrenia.
Catatonia is a disturbance of movement in which a person may remain motionless for hours or move without purpose.
A delusion is a false belief, often of persecution or grandeur, that a person holds despite clear evidence against it.
Correct. Flat affect is a lack of emotional expression in the face and voice.

questions.explanation: Flat affect is a lack of emotional expression in the face and voice.

questions.stem: After a poor exam result, Bea feels better when she thinks about classmates who scored lower. Which process is this?

options.why: The mere exposure effect is the tendency to like something more simply because we have encountered it repeatedly.
Correct. Downward social comparison is the comparing of oneself with people who are doing worse.
A situational attribution is an explanation of behavior that points to outside circumstances.
An external locus of control is the belief that outcomes are decided by luck, fate or other people.

questions.explanation: Downward social comparison is the comparing of oneself with people who are doing worse.

questions.title: Article analysis: a study of reaction time

parts.prompt: Identify the research method used in the study.

rubric.criterion: Identifies the method as an experiment.
rubric.example: The study is an experiment: the researchers manipulated a variable and randomly assigned the subjects to conditions.

parts.prompt: State the operational definition of reaction time.

rubric.criterion: States how the variable was measured in this study.
rubric.example: Reaction time was defined as the average time in milliseconds that each participant took to press a button when a light appeared.

parts.prompt: Describe the meaning of the difference between the two group averages.

rubric.criterion: Accurately describes which group scored higher or lower and what that means for the variable measured.
rubric.example: The group that stayed awake responded more slowly. On average, the value was 412 for the group that stayed awake all night and 318 for the group that slept for eight hours, and a p value of 0.01 means a difference this large is unlikely to be due to chance.

parts.prompt: Identify at least one ethical guideline applied by the researchers.

rubric.criterion: Identifies an ethical guideline that the summary shows was followed.
rubric.example: Informed consent: participants agreed to take part after being told about the study. (Also acceptable: debriefing; the right to withdraw; approval by an institutional review board.)

parts.prompt: Explain the extent to which the research findings may or may not be generalizable, using specific and relevant evidence from the study.

rubric.criterion: Explains a limit (or strength) of generalizability with reference to the sample.
rubric.example: The sample was 60 adult volunteers from one city, so the findings may not apply to people of other ages, cultures or backgrounds. Because the sample was not randomly selected from a wider population, it may not be representative.

parts.prompt: Explain how at least one of the research findings supports or refutes the researchers' hypothesis.

rubric.criterion: Uses a specific finding from the study as evidence.
rubric.example: The group that stayed awake responded more slowly. (412 compared with 318).

rubric.criterion: Explains how the finding supports the hypothesis, using a psychological concept.
rubric.example: This supports the hypothesis that the amount of sleep affects reaction time. Because subjects were randomly assigned, the difference can be attributed to the amount of sleep. The finding illustrates sleep restores the brain, so sleep loss impairs attention and reaction time.

questions.title: Evidence-based question: Does heavy social media use harm the well-being of teenagers?

parts.prompt: Propose a specific and defensible claim, based in psychological science, that responds to the question.

rubric.criterion: States a claim that answers the question and can be supported by the sources.
rubric.example: Heavy social media use can harm teenagers' well-being, especially when it leads them to compare themselves with others.

parts.prompt: (i) Support your claim using at least one piece of specific and relevant evidence from one of the sources. (ii) Explain how the evidence supports your claim, using a psychological perspective, theory, concept or research finding learned in AP Psychology.

rubric.criterion: Uses specific, relevant evidence from one source and names the source.
rubric.example: In Source B, students who limited social media to 30 minutes a day had lower loneliness scores (38) than students who continued as usual (45).

rubric.criterion: Explains how the evidence supports the claim.
rubric.example: This supports the claim because the study was an experiment with random assignment, so reducing social media use can be said to have caused the lower loneliness. Less time online leaves more time for face-to-face contact, which supports well-being.

rubric.criterion: Correctly applies a psychological concept in the explanation.
rubric.example: The concept must be named and applied correctly, as in the model explanation.

parts.prompt: (i) Support your claim using an additional piece of specific and relevant evidence from a different source. (ii) Explain how this evidence supports your claim, using a different psychological perspective, theory, concept or research finding.

rubric.criterion: Uses specific, relevant evidence from a different source and names the source.
rubric.example: In Source C, many teenagers said they felt worse about themselves after viewing images of peers who seemed more attractive or popular.

rubric.criterion: Explains how the evidence supports the claim.
rubric.example: This supports the claim through upward social comparison and relative deprivation: comparing oneself with people who seem better off lowers self-esteem and satisfaction.

rubric.criterion: Correctly applies a different psychological concept from the one used in part B.
rubric.example: The concept must differ from the one used in part B and be applied correctly.
